brief: Verdict ahead of the print: leadership continuity and the size of Nvidia's ecosystem guarantees matter more than the revenue beat.
Kona: do not rely on Nvidia backstops in a GPU-owner tenant's financing plan.
changes: Report date: Tuesday 17 November, results about 1:20 p.m. PT, call 2:00 p.m. PT (company, 28 October; repeated in the 12 November release filed as 8-K ex. 99.1).

Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, president and director (effective 11 November, announced 12 November; no reason given in the 8-K). CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO and stays CFO; Harvey Jones becomes the first-ever board chair; the board expects operations, customer commitments and roadmap to continue without interruption. On 8 November the board had opened an independent investigation with outside counsel (company statement, per press).
Downgrades: Bernstein to Market Perform on CEO uncertainty ($400 to $200); Baird to Neutral on data center visibility and supply ($500 to $200); Wells Fargo target $315 to $300 (press).

The Information (reported 23 October) put Nvidia's exposure to neoclouds at more than $170bn; Nvidia reported in talks on a residual value guarantee for Nscale's West Virginia campus for Anthropic (The Information, 29 October).
Bloomberg (5 November): Microsoft pulling back from parts of deals with Nscale, Nebius and IREN.
checks: Built before results. Date from Nvidia's 28 October release, repeated in the 12 November release (8-K ex. 99.1). CEO transition from the 8-K (items 5.02, 9.01; event date 11 November; no reason stated). 2Q FY27 figures and 3Q guide from release and CFO commentary; guarantees ($108.5bn incl. $105bn Ohio), cloud ($29bn) and AI-cloud ($36bn) agreements, equity ($99bn held, $25bn committed), supply commitments ($279bn), DSO and 16% customer from the 2Q 10-Q; all confirmed by a fresh subagent. Consensus: ~$109bn revenue and $2.47 EPS confirmed; LSEG $109.2bn, Fiscal AI $108.4bn, ranges and FY27/FY28 not reopened. Price $173.73 (11 Nov) confirmed; record close $239.11 (CoinAlertNews) vs $239.24 unconfirmed; drawdown ~27% computed. Removed: Oppenheimer downgrade, -10% intraday move and FBI probe (unsourced); personal allegations not stated. Single-source: China $7.5bn, Firmus, OpenAI tranche, Baird write-down, H200s in Hong Kong. No CDS level for November.
consensus_thesis: Investors own Nvidia for supply-constrained AI demand (FY28 revenue guided up about 70%) and 74-75% gross margins, and have grown wary of the balance sheet it lends to the ecosystem (about $108.5bn of guarantees, $65bn of cloud and AI-cloud capacity agreements, about $99bn of equity stakes); at $173.73 on 11 November, before the resignation was announced, the stock was about 27% below its 6 October record close (~$239), so it now prices leadership and vendor-financing risk, not a demand problem.
headline: Fiscal 3Q27 (quarter to 25 October, results 17 November after the close) is a test of whether the $108bn revenue guide, $422bn of commitments and $108.5bn of guarantees still look safe after Jensen Huang resigned as CEO (effective 11 November, announced 12 November).
kona: Nvidia's guarantees and capacity buy-backs are what make many neocloud tenants financeable; if the CEO change or the Microsoft pull-back makes Nvidia cap that support, GPU-owning tenants lose a backstop and lenders will price their credit on its own. Kona should not count on Nvidia credit support in a GPU-owner tenant's financing plan, and should prefer tenants whose contracts are backed by a hyperscaler or prepaid.

questions.question: The 2Q 10-Q lists $108.5bn of guarantees, $105bn of it for the Ohio campus leased to an OpenAI affiliate, and $36bn of AI-cloud capacity agreements. What were both at 25 October, which counterparties do they cover, and what has been drawn or reserved?
questions.why: Tests how much neocloud and lab credit risk sits on Nvidia's balance sheet.

questions.question: Press reports Nvidia is weighing a residual value guarantee for Nscale's West Virginia campus. Has any new guarantee or capacity purchase been signed since July, and is there a cap the board has set on such support?
DSO rose to 60 days from 45 on extended terms for investment-grade customers. What were DSO and receivables at quarter-end, and are any neocloud receivables past due?

With Microsoft reportedly pulling back from parts of its Nscale, Nebius and IREN deals, have any AI-cloud customers deferred or cancelled Blackwell or Rubin orders, and does the 4Q guide assume any capacity Nvidia itself buys back?
questions.why: Tests demand durability through the neocloud channel.

questions.question: Under interim leadership, are the FY28 ~70% growth outlook and the gross-margin path (71-72% trough in 4Q, 72-73% in FY28) reaffirmed?
questions.why: Tests whether guidance survives the CEO change.

questions.question: The Information reported about $7.5bn of Nvidia chips reaching China (single source). Is any revenue at risk of restatement, write-down or export penalty?
questions.why: Legal and compliance tail on reported revenue.

risks: Leadership transition; the board's independent investigation (company statement, 8 November); circumstances not stated in the 8-K.
Vendor financing: guarantees and capacity agreements with neoclouds and labs called on if a customer fails.
China export compliance (reports of chips reaching China; H200 units stuck in Hong Kong).
Gross margin squeezed by memory prices.

sections.body: Buyer and financier mode: Nvidia sells the GPUs, and increasingly supports demand for them by investing in labs and neoclouds, buying back cloud capacity, and guaranteeing leases and land. Data center was $89.0bn of $96.2bn 2Q FY27 revenue. One direct customer was 16% of 2Q revenue.
